## `espn_nba_teams`

```python
espn_nba_teams(return_as_pandas: bool = False, **kwargs) -> pl.DataFrame
```

The full NBA team directory from ESPN's Site v2 API.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `return_as_pandas` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, return a pandas DataFrame; else polars. |

**Returns** — a tidy `polars.DataFrame`, one row per team (same tidy column set as
every other league's `espn_<sport>_teams`).

**Example**

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams

teams = espn_nba_teams()
print("shape:", teams.shape)
teams.select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]).head(10)
```

## `espn_nba_team_roster`

```python
espn_nba_team_roster(team_id: int | str, *, return_parsed: bool = True,
                     return_as_pandas: bool = False, **kwargs) -> pl.DataFrame | dict
```

A single team's roster. Parser-backed, so `return_parsed=True` is the default.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `team_id` | `int \| str` | — | ESPN team identifier (e.g. `13` for the Los Angeles Lakers). |
| `return_parsed` | `bool` | `True` | If `True`, return a tidy frame; `False` for the raw `Dict`. |
| `return_as_pandas` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, return a pandas DataFrame. |

**Returns** — a tidy `polars.DataFrame`, one row per athlete; or the raw ESPN
`Dict` when `return_parsed=False`.

**Example**

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_team_roster

roster = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13)
print("shape:", roster.shape)
cols = [c for c in roster.columns if "name" in c.lower() or "position" in c.lower()][:5]
roster.select(cols).head(8) if cols else roster.head(8)
```

The raw form, for comparison:

```{python}
raw = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13, return_parsed=False)
print("raw type:", type(raw).__name__)
print("top-level keys:", list(raw.keys())[:8])
```

## `espn_nba_scoreboard`

```python
espn_nba_scoreboard(dates: int | str | None = None, *,
                    return_as_pandas: bool = False, **kwargs) -> pl.DataFrame
```

The scoreboard for a given date (`YYYYMMDD`).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dates` | `int \| str` | `None` | Date in `YYYYMMDD`; defaults to today. |
| `return_as_pandas` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, return a pandas DataFrame. |

**Returns** — a tidy `polars.DataFrame`, one row per game on the slate.

**Example**

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_scoreboard

sb = espn_nba_scoreboard(dates="20240115")   # a settled 2024 date
print("shape:", sb.shape)
keep = [c for c in ["id", "name", "short_name", "status_type_detail"] if c in sb.columns]
sb.select(keep).head(6)
```

::: {.callout-note}
For the R analogue of these functions, see
[`hoopR`](https://hoopR.sportsdataverse.org) — the SportsDataverse maintains a
near-identical surface across Python and R.
:::
